mentions.name: Layman-Friendly Quantum Computing Book
mentions.description: A free, extended blog post-style book that explains quantum computing to a layman-ish but technically minded audience. It covers the computational theory, the actual hardware implementations, and the potential applications of quantum computers, and aims to be unbiased and steer away from misleading industry hype. Work in progress for about six months.
mentions.problem: Educational material on quantum computing is either too academic, too narrow in scope, or totally facile, leaving no accessible on-ramp for technically minded people to follow a hyped field.
mentions.audience: Technically minded lay readers who want to understand quantum computing without being quantum physicists.
mentions.source_excerpt: I've been writing a 'book' (more of an extended blog post that I'd like to put out for free) attempting to explain quantum computing to a layman-ish audience.

evidence.value: I've been writing a 'book' (more of an extended blog post that I'd like to put out for free) attempting to explain quantum computing to a layman-ish audience.
